findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 2, Harm 4
Raise: Security — The ruling excluded project and local settings to prevent hooks, but this line still loads user settings. Claude's [hook documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#security-considerations) confirms that user-level hooks run with the user's full permissions; that source was not addressed by the ruling. Case: normal use - A developer has a global SessionStart hook that runs a checkout's setup or formatter. A Claude ask starts that hook against the real checkout, where it can overwrite uncommitted edits before the answer.
findings.title: Disputed keep 12: User hooks still run during Claude's read-only turn

findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 2, Harm 4
Raise: Security — The deny list removes three built-in tools but leaves configured MCP tools available. The [pinned SDK](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/v0.2.187/src/claude_agent_sdk/types.py) defaults `strict_mcp_config` to false, and Claude's [permission rules](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/permissions) allow pre-approved MCP tools to run. Case: normal use - A developer has a globally pre-approved filesystem MCP server and asks Claude about a checkout; its write tool can modify an edited file despite the read-only promise. This MCP route is separate from the Bash, Edit and Write tools covered by the ruling.

findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 1, Harm 4
Raise: Security — The Codex failure branch ignores the safe `again` text and embeds the question using JSON double quotes. Case: normal use - A developer asks about a shell expression containing `$(...)` or backticks, then pastes the suggested retry; the shell executes the substitution. The retry also drops an explicit `--model`, so retrying a Codex ask from a Codex session can ask Claude instead.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done — The Gemini path calls `antigravity.read`, which requires the pinned Autoreview helper at `src/forge/antigravity.py:288`; `src/forge/review.py:797` refuses when it is absent or has another version. Case: normal use - A new repo has Antigravity installed and signed in, as the accepted limit requires, but has not installed this separate review helper. A Gemini ask refuses before starting instead of printing and recording an answer. The new test supplies the helper explicitly at `tests/test_ask_command.py:118`, so it misses this setup.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 4
Raise: Test — The checkout comparison makes only the Gemini stub attempt a write. The Claude stub exercises neither user hooks nor MCP tools, while `test_3` asserts the settings that leave those routes open. The Codex failure test uses only `Q` and no explicit model, so it also passes with the unsafe, family-changing retry shown by the current code. Case: normal use - A Claude ask overwrites an edit through a user hook or MCP tool, or a developer copies a Codex retry containing shell substitution; the named proof still passes.

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test — The per-family case passes the Gemini model explicitly and checks only its effort. No named proof asks without `--model` while using a per-family entry, so the tests would pass if configured per-family model names were ignored. Case: normal use - A Codex session has `[models.ask.claude]` set to a specific Claude model, but a bare ask uses Claude's default instead.

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test — The wait case exercises only Codex, and the Codex test checks its answer on stdout without checking the work log. The Claude and Gemini cases do not check waiting. Case: normal use - Claude or Gemini starts while every agent place is occupied, or a Codex answer is printed but not recorded; the named tests would still pass.
